Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: production transparent sprite animation atlas for an original Chinese myth HD-2D game.
Input image is a CHARACTER IDENTITY AND PAINTING STYLE REFERENCE ONLY. Preserve this male traveler with brown high ponytail, jade teal layered coat, ivory scarf, dark pants and brown boots. Make a NEW atlas of the SAME character with clear fluid animation poses.
EXACT layout: 6 equal columns by 4 equal rows, exactly 24 separate full body figures. Large high resolution square canvas. Every figure stays wholly inside its cell with transparent gutters. Consistent body size, fixed pelvis center and ground baseline within cells; full hair, hands and feet visible.
Rows 1 and 2 both show ONLY front facing viewer. Rows 3 and 4 both show ONLY front-right three-quarter facing diagonally toward the viewer's right. These are true distinct camera views, including the actual back design when specified, not mirrored frontal images. No turning during a row.
Row 1: six sequential WALK CYCLE frames in the first view: left contact, down, passing, right contact, down, passing. Natural opposite arm/leg swing, feet alternate, cloth and scarf trail gently; all six frames actually different, loop returns smoothly.
Row 2: six consecutive ATTACK frames in the first view: neutral guard, torso anticipation, accelerating swing, fully extended strike, follow-through, recover. The right hand grips an invisible hilt; left arm balances. UNARMED artwork because the engine attaches a weapon, absolutely no drawn sword or staff, no magic particles or trails. Keep body proportions and face identical across frames.
Row 3: same six-step walk sequence in second view. Row 4: same six-step attack sequence in second view.
Style: warm detailed Japanese anime chibi watercolor illustration, clean hand painted outlines, 3 heads tall, natural human anatomy, identical lighting and costume throughout, isolated real transparent alpha background. No floor, drop shadows, grid lines, labels, text, numbers, border, scenery, extra people, duplicate cells, or cropping. Prioritize readable sequential limbs and exact atlas arrangement over tiny ornaments.
